To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the performance of dense stereo algorithms in real-world automotive environment imagery is different from the performance of the same algorithms in standard dense stereo evaluation test sequences.
the performance of a dense stereo algorithm in a real-world application such as an automotive environment is not necessarily the same as its performance on a standard test set.

(i) the quality of disparity maps produced by complex stereo algorithms can be significantly degraded by noise present in the automotive environment, (ii) this noise has a greater effect than the complexity of the stereo algorithm and (iii) the disparity maps produced by simpler stereo algorithms (Block Matching, Semi- Global Matching) are of comparable quality to the more complex algorithms (Semi-Global Matching, Cross-Based Local, Adaptive Aggregation Dynamic Programming) in an automotive environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
evaluating the suitability of real-time dense stereovision for automotive application.
evaluating the performance of several state of the art real-time stereo algorithms for use in an automotive environment.
the evaluation of dense stereo algorithms in the context of the automotive environment, and the impact of the noise found in automotive imagery on the performance of the algorithms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best algorithm depends on the environment and application.
the Semi-Global Matching algorithm provides the best empirical performance for automotive environment imagery.
the performance of the algorithms in the automotive environment is dependent on the nature of the input data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the best algorithm for automotive application dense stereo is Semi-Global Matching with Block Matching as a close second, however, the performance of the other algorithms are still comparable.
for automotive applications, a Semi-Global approach is the best option for dense stereo.

for dense stereo algorithms, in order to obtain a reliable performance in real world scenarios (such as those found in automotive applications) it is important to consider the algorithm performance on real data, as well as the standard test sequences, and also the computational requirements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a real-time dense stereo algorithm should be chosen with consideration of its performance in a specific application environment.
the performance of the stereo algorithms is highly dependent on the environment in which the algorithm is applied and the test sequences that are used to benchmark the algorithms.
the use of real-world data in the comparative evaluation of dense stereo algorithms is important to ensure a robust comparison.
